title: Work & Career Collocations
grammarTitle: Work & Career Collocations — Words That Go Together
grammarNote: В профессиональном английском языке существуют устойчивые словосочетания (collocations), которые нельзя заменять синонимами. "Apply FOR a job" — нельзя говорить "apply to a job." "Make progress" — нельзя говорить "do progress." Эти сочетания нужно запомнить как единицы.

grammarTable.subject: apply for
grammarTable.verb: apply for a job / position / scholarship
grammarTable.example: "I applied for three internships this week." / "She applied for the scholarship."

grammarTable.subject: get / receive
grammarTable.example: "He got a promotion last year." / "She received a pay raise."

grammarTable.subject: make
grammarTable.verb: make progress / a decision / a mistake
grammarTable.example: "She's been making progress." / "I made a mistake — I'll fix it."

grammarTable.subject: take
grammarTable.example: "He takes responsibility for his team." / "Take a break at 1 pm."

grammarTable.subject: do
grammarTable.example: "She's doing an internship at DataBridge." / "He does research in AI."

grammarTable.subject: have
grammarTable.verb: have experience / a meeting / an impact
grammarTable.example: "Do you have experience with Python?" / "We're having a meeting at 3."

rows.example: "I applied FOR a software engineer position." ✅ NOT "apply to" or "apply a job."

rows.form: get a job / an offer / a promotion
rows.example: "She got a job at DataBridge." / "Did you get the offer?" ✅
"It's hard to find a job after graduation." ✅ "Find" collocates with "job" naturally.
"She landed a great job at a tech startup!" ✅ (informal = get a desirable job)

grammarExtra.title: Make, do, take — common work collocations

rows.form: make: progress / a decision / a mistake / money / time
rows.example: "MAKE progress." / "MAKE a decision." / "MAKE a mistake." / "MAKE money." ✅

rows.form: do: research / overtime / an internship / a course
rows.example: "DO research." / "DO overtime." / "DO an internship." / "DO a course." ✅

rows.form: take: responsibility / a break / notes / action

rows.example: ✗ "do progress" → ✅ "make progress." ✗ "make research" → ✅ "do research." ✗ "take a mistake" → ✅ "make a mistake."
"Do you have experience WITH Python?" / "She has experience IN project management." ✅
"I'm doing an internship to gain experience." ✅ (acquire experience)
"She's been building her skills in machine learning." ✅ (gradually develop)
"He's been developing his communication skills." ✅ (grow and improve)
"She got a promotion to Senior Engineer after two years." ✅
"He asked for a pay raise and received one." ✅
"She's been climbing the career ladder quickly." ✅ (getting more senior positions)
"She resigned from her position." / "He quit his job." ✅
"He was made redundant when the company downsized." ✅ (lost job due to company cuts)

grammarTip:
Work & Career collocations — не путай:

APPLY FOR (не to, не a):
"Apply FOR a job / scholarship" ✅

MAKE: progress / a decision / a mistake / money
DO: research / overtime / an internship / a course
TAKE: responsibility / a break / notes / action

⚠️ Ловушки:
✗ "do progress" → ✅ "make progress"
✗ "make research" → ✅ "do research"
✗ "take a mistake" → ✅ "make a mistake"
✗ "apply to a job" → ✅ "apply FOR a job"

Последовательность карьеры:
get a job → gain experience → make progress
→ get a promotion → climb the career ladder

exercises.text: She ___ a job at DataBridge Solutions after her internship.
exercises.hint: "GET a job." ✅ Not "make a job" or "do a job." You get / find / land a job.

exercises.text: I ___ for three internships this month. I'm waiting to hear back.
exercises.hint: "APPLY FOR an internship/job." ✅ You apply for positions.

exercises.text: She's been ___ a lot of progress since she started the course.
He's ___ an internship at the Ministry of Education this summer.
exercises.hint: "DO an internship." ✅ Also: "do a course / do overtime / do research."

exercises.text: In meetings, I always ___ notes so I don't forget anything.
exercises.hint: "TAKE notes." ✅ Also: "take a break / take responsibility / take action."

exercises.text: "She's been ___ experience in project management over the past year."
exercises.hint: "GAIN experience." ✅ = acquire or develop. "She's been GAINING experience." ✅

exercises.text: Do you have experience ___ Python and machine learning?
exercises.hint: "have experience WITH [tool/skill]." ✅ "Have experience WITH Python." OR "experience IN [field]." ✅

exercises.text: "She did a big mistake in the report." — What is wrong?
exercises.hint: ✅ "She MADE a big mistake." — "make a mistake." NEVER "do a mistake."

exercises.text: After five years, she finally ___ a promotion to Senior Manager.
exercises.hint: "GET a promotion." ✅ Also: "receive a promotion." NOT "make" or "do" a promotion.

exercises.text: He needs to ___ responsibility for the project outcomes.
exercises.hint: "TAKE responsibility." ✅ Also: "take notes / take a break / take action."

exercises.instruction: Complete with the correct collocation verb.
exercises.text: "She ___ research into renewable energy for her thesis."
exercises.hint: "DO research." ✅ Also: "do overtime / do a course / do an internship." NEVER "make research."

exercises.text: "She left her job last month." — Formal equivalent:
exercises.hint: "RESIGN FROM a position/job." ✅ Formal equivalent of "quit." "She RESIGNED FROM her position." ✅

questions.text: "She applied ___ a senior position." Correct preposition:
questions.hint: "apply FOR a job/position." ✅ Always "apply FOR" — never "apply to" or "apply a job."

questions.text: "He ___ a lot of progress this year." Choose.
"She's ___ an internship at a tech firm." Choose.
questions.hint: "DO an internship." ✅ Also: do research / do overtime / do a course.

questions.text: "___ notes in every meeting." Correct verb:
questions.hint: "TAKE notes." ✅ Also: "take a break / take responsibility / take action."

questions.text: "You need to ___ responsibility for your decisions." (accept it)
"He got a ___ after two years of excellent performance."
questions.hint: "GET a promotion." ✅ = move to a higher position.

questions.text: "She made a mistake." — Which verb is WRONG with "mistake"?
questions.hint: ✅ "MAKE a mistake." NEVER "DO a mistake." The verb is always "make" with "mistake."

questions.text: "Do you have experience ___ Python?" Correct preposition:

questions.hint: "DEVELOP skills." ✅ = grow and improve over time. Also: "build skills." ✅

questions.text: "I applied ___ the scholarship and got it!" (preposition)
questions.hint: "apply FOR a scholarship / job / position." ✅ Always "FOR."

questions.text: "She does ___ every week to finish the project."
questions.hint: "DO overtime." ✅ = work extra hours beyond normal time. "She does overtime every week."

questions.text: "She's been ___ experience as a team leader." (gaining it)

questions.hint: "resign FROM a position/job." ✅ "He RESIGNED FROM his position." ✅

questions.text: "She ___ a big mistake in the report." Choose correctly.
questions.hint: "MAKE a mistake." ✅ Always "make" — never "do a mistake."

opts: both with and in are correct
questions.correct: both with and in are correct
questions.hint: "experience IN project management" (field) ✅ / "experience WITH project management tools" (specific). Both patterns work! ✅
"applied FOR the internship." ✅ Others: "made progress" ✅, "did research" ✅, "made a mistake" ✅.
